report.summary: Reviewed languages.py chunk 1: defines LanguageSpec dataclass, _rx helper, _SPECS tuple with 20 languages, SPECS dict, and spec_for function. Docstring claims about backends, comment stripping, and document spec registry are partially uncheckable.
risks: docstring line 16 | medium | Claim that string_delims default covers C family but Rust and Swift override; Rust override is present, Swift override is present, but claim 'Default covers the C family' is accurate for the default. No risk.
docstring line 48 | low | Claim that node-type names follow tree-sitter grammar; cannot verify against actual grammar files, but naming convention looks plausible.
docstring line 122 | medium | Claim that spec_for is not a lookup table but a claim; this is confusing and may mislead. The code shows it is a simple dict lookup, so the claim is misleading.
docstring line 124-138 | high | Claim about thirteen call sites and their behavior; none of those call sites are present in this chunk, so the claim is uncheckable. Relies on code outside chunk.

handoff.purpose: Define LanguageSpec dataclass and populate the language registry with 20 language definitions.

symbols.name: LanguageSpec
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with fields: name, extensions, line_comment, block_comment, string_delims, ts_grammar, function_types, import_types, guard_keywords, safety_content.

symbols.name: _rx
symbols.note: Helper to compile regex patterns into tuple of re.Pattern.

symbols.name: _SPECS
symbols.note: Tuple of 20 LanguageSpec instances for languages: python, c, cpp, java, rust, go, javascript, typescript, csharp, qml, css, qss, scss, kotlin, swift, ruby, php, lua, shell.

symbols.name: SPECS
symbols.note: dict[str, LanguageSpec] mapping lowercase extension to LanguageSpec, built from _SPECS.

symbols.name: spec_for
symbols.note: Returns LanguageSpec for given path by extension, or None if unsupported.

claims.text: Adding a language is *data*, not code: one ``LanguageSpec`` entry.

claims.why: No code in this chunk shows backends consuming these fields.
No tree-sitter backend code is present in this chunk.

claims.why: No safety fence code is present in this chunk.

claims.text: Default covers the C family; override where ' is not a string opener -- Rust lifetimes ('a) and Swift, where consuming to the next ' would eat code.
claims.why: Rust spec sets string_delims=('"',) (single quote excluded), Swift spec sets string_delims=('"',) (single quote excluded). Default is ('"', "'").

claims.text: Node-type names follow the corresponding tree-sitter grammar; they are only read when tree-sitter is installed.
claims.why: No tree-sitter grammar files or usage code in this chunk.

claims.text: A DocumentSpec is NOT a LanguageSpec and ``.md`` is deliberately NOT added to ``SPECS``. ``spec_for`` is not a lookup table, it is a CLAIM, and thirteen call sites read it as one: ...
claims.why: No DocumentSpec or call sites are present in this chunk. spec_for is a simple dict lookup in this chunk, so the 'claim' statement is misleading but cannot be fully verified.

observations.what: The docstring claims three backends consume the fields, but no backend code is present in this chunk.
The docstring claims spec_for is not a lookup table but a claim, yet the implementation is a simple dict lookup (SPECS.get). This is contradictory.
The docstring lists thirteen call sites and their behavior, none of which are present in this chunk.
The comment about string_delims default covering C family and overrides for Rust and Swift is accurate: Rust and Swift specs explicitly set string_delims to exclude single quote.
The _SPECS tuple includes 20 languages, each with varying fields; some languages lack certain fields (e.g., css has no line_comment or guard_keywords).
